contexts.text: It treats concerning those who have external worship, in which are interior evils and falsities. Nimrod = such worship.

By Nimrod () are signified those who made internal worship external; and thus by Nimrod is signified such external worship... To make internal worship external is to make external worship essential rather than internal... Such is the religion of those who separate faith from charity, in that they prefer... the things which are of the Knowledges of faith to those which are of the life; thus formal things to essential ones. Explained.
Such worship is called Nimrod; and it is born of the Knowledges which are Cash; as these are from faith separated from charity, which faith is Ham.

Cush begat Nimrod () = that those who had Knowledges of interior things instituted such worship... Knowledges of interior things are what they call doctrines... It is those who call mere Knowledges faith, who beget and institute such worship...
He was a mighty one in the earth () = that such religion prevailed in the Church.
He was mighty in hunting before Jehovah () = that it has persuaded many; (for) faith separated from charity is such. Explained.

Wherefore it was said, As Nimrod mighty in hunting before Jehovah () = that because so many were persuaded, such a form of speech became proverbial... As, in ancient times, they gave names to Things, they gave this name to this worship, saying that Nimrod was mighty in hunting, that is, was one which captivates minds...

And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar () = that there were such worships... the externals of which appear holy, but the interiors are profane.
That such worship reasons about spiritual and celestial things, (is signified by) Nimrod went forth from that land into Asshur, or Assyria.
The land of Nimrod () = such worship as that which is signified by Nimrod, in which the interiors are evil and false.
